facts.text: The README describes a ROS Noetic package for a Panda Emika Franka Gazebo simulation that wraps the franka_ros and panda_moveit_config packages.
start_simulation.launch defaults the world to empty.world and control_type to trajectory.
The launch starts a node named panda_control_server and, for trajectory control, loads the arm follow-joint-trajectory action instead of the set_joint_commands service.
PandaControlServer creates a SimpleActionServer of type FollowJointTrajectoryAction on the relative name formed from the last component of its node name and '/panda_arm/follow_joint_trajectory'.

The action goal declares trajectory, path_tolerance, goal_tolerance, goal_time_tolerance, create_time_axis, time_axis_step and timeout, whose comment says a timeout of 0 waits indefinitely; the result declares error_code and error_string.
The server connects a SimpleActionClient of type control_msgs FollowJointTrajectoryAction to the relative action name panda_arm_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory when that server exists.
The execute callback sends the converted goal through that client, waits for the result with goal.timeout, and aborts with error_code -6 when the wait does not finish.
The wrapper succeeds only when its preempt flag is false and the forwarded controller result has error_code SUCCESSFUL; otherwise it aborts with the forwarded result.
The preempt callback cancels the forwarded controller goal when it is active or preempting and then marks the wrapper goal preempted, without waiting for the controller's terminal result.
PandaControlServer creates the SetGripperWidth service on the relative name formed from the last component of its node name and '/panda_hand/set_gripper_width' when the gripper is loaded.

The gripper callback halves the requested width, clips the result to [0, 0.08], puts it in a GripperCommandGoal's command.position with the request's max_effort (or GRASP_FORCE when that is 0 and grasping is true, else 0), and sends the goal when the gripper client is connected.
load_panda_joint_limits sets the finger joint limits of panda_finger_joint1 and panda_finger_joint2 to 0.0 and 0.04.

The gripper callback waits for the gripper action result only when wait is true, using the request timeout; otherwise it sets success true after sending the goal; without a connected gripper client it sets success false.
SetGripperWidth.srv declares width, grasping, max_effort, wait and timeout, and returns success and message.
GRASP_FORCE is 10, and its comment states the Panda continuous force is 70 N and max_force is 140 N.
The arm joint names are panda_joint1 through panda_joint7 and the hand names are panda_finger_joint1 and panda_finger_joint2.
PandaControlServer subscribes to the relative topic 'joint_states' with JointState messages.
The Gazebo world plugin's SERVICE_NAME constant is the absolute name /lock_unlock_panda_joints.
The plugin's Load creates a node handle named panda_joint_control_plugin and advertises SERVICE_NAME on it with the LockUnlockJoints callback.

The callback looks up the Gazebo model named by MODEL_NAME and returns success false when it is missing; it returns success false at the first missing joint without restoring the joints it has already handled.

For lock true the callback stores each joint's present lower and upper limits and sets both limits to the joint's current position; for lock false it restores the stored limits when both exist; it then returns success true. It reads no joint velocity.
The plugin's MODEL_NAME constant is panda.
LockJoints.srv declares joint_names and lock in the request and success and message in the response.
The shipped empty.world loads the panda_joint_locker plugin from libpanda_gazebo.so.
The package declares the MIT licence.

determinism.notes: Event-driven wire stand-in with no physics step, no controller interpolation, no action feedback and no wall-clock pacing; the placeholder joint values do not establish state-hash replay

gaps: the fake answers the declared /joint_states subscription, the wrapper trajectory action, the gripper width service and the lock service without Gazebo, franka_gazebo, ros_control, MoveIt or a ROS graph
trajectory goals complete instantly with a canned error_code; there is no interpolation, controller latency, feedback, collision, gravity or controller error behavior
gripper commands record the requested total width and force but run no franka_gripper action, contact or grasp; the accepted result only says the goal was sent
the lock service records the request and reports success; it does not run Gazebo joint-limit enforcement, so a fake stop is not physical or measured quiescence

all joint samples, widths, forces and goal identifiers are placeholders, not device facts or limits; a live run needs the operator's Gazebo, ros_control controllers, franka_gripper and rosbridge deployment
the upstream /joint_states publisher order, the real joint travel limits (in the franka_ros submodule), controller timing and every physical stop latency are not established here

every lock request stores the joint's present limits as the limits an unlock restores (panda_joint_locker_world_plugin.cpp:93-111); a reviewer probe of this fake showed the runtime sending the lock twice for an idle e-stop, four times for an e-stop with a trajectory goal in flight and three times for an ordinary trajectory cancellation, so an upstream unlock afterwards restores the locked limits and the simulated arm stays frozen until the model is respawned or Gazebo restarts; the package declares no unlock and mhs.safety.reset does not unlock

the upstream gripper clip allows 0.08 m per finger (control_server.py:1466-1472), twice the finger joint limit the clone states (helpers.py:613-621); franka_gazebo's gripper simulation in the franka_ros submodule (outside the pinned object store) refuses a per-finger position above 0.04 m while the wrapper with wait false still reports success, so the finger_width limit is the clone's 0.04 m finger limit rather than the clip; even with wait true the wrapper's success is the return of wait_for_result (control_server.py:1491-1494), which says the goal finished, not that it succeeded

the shipped launch starts MoveIt (demo.launch with the simple controller manager), the panda_moveit_planner_server and RViz by default (put_robot_in_world.launch:10, 53-61, 80-86, 101-105); they can command the same controllers outside MHS, the MHS latch does not fence them, and only the lock constrains them

/joint_states comes from franka_ros's joint_state_publisher on simulated time (outside the pinned object store); while Gazebo is paused it is silent, and a reviewer probe with the topic silent showed mhs.resource.read failing MHS.DEVICE.NOT_READY after 2 s and each command waiting about 2 s for that read before completing; the e-stop was not delayed

the wrapper action and gripper service target the generic controller names panda_arm_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory and franka_gripper/gripper_action (control_server.py:266-277, 341-348), not a Gazebo-only interface; run against a real Franka graph (franka_control in the franka_ros submodule) they would move a real arm, while the lock service, a Gazebo world plugin, would be absent and every e-stop would fail with the latch held

the lock relies on the Gazebo physics engine enforcing joint limits; the launch offers ode or dart physics (start_simulation.launch:11-12), and that enforcement is outside the clone and not verified here

safe_state.description: Every Panda arm and finger joint has its Gazebo lower and upper limits set to the position it had when the /lock_unlock_panda_joints callback ran. The service acknowledges that limit update, not a measured zero velocity; Gazebo keeps running, and the trajectory controller, MoveIt or any other ROS client may keep commanding the locked joints. The lock persists after mhs.safety.reset: no unlock is declared, and repeated lock requests overwrite the limits the plugin stores for an unlock.
